ruleName: Ball Moved by Natural Forces / Ball Stopped by Player’s Equipment
title: Ball Moved by Wind and Stopped by Measuring Club
question: You place a club on the ground to measure a relief area. Before you continue, your ball is moved by wind and rolls until it comes to rest against the club you laid on the ground. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: No penalty. Play the ball from where it now lies against the club.
No penalty. Move the club and replace the ball on its original spot.
One-stroke penalty for stopping the ball with your equipment.
You must drop the ball again.

explanation: Although the wind caused the ball to move, your club deliberately placed on the ground stopped the ball from continuing to move. The ball must be replaced on its original spot with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: Ball Blown by Wind and Stopped by Your Club on the Ground
juniorVersion.question: You put your club on the ground to see how far you can drop your ball. Before you do anything else, the wind blows your ball and it rolls until it hits your club and stops. What should you do?

choices.text: No penalty. Play the ball from where it stopped by the club.
No penalty. Move your club and put the ball back where it was before it moved.
One-shot penalty because your club stopped the ball.
You must drop the ball again.

juniorVersion.explanation: Your club on the ground stopped your ball after the wind moved it. There is no penalty, but you must move your club and put the ball back where it was before.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The area where you are allowed to drop your ball.
Put the ball back where it was before it moved.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children how to carefully put the ball back where it started if it is moved by wind and stopped by something you placed on the ground.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they should play from where the ball stopped.
They might think there is a penalty because the club stopped the ball.
